_note: Sixteen curated generation seeds, chosen off a 48-seed parity sweep on 2026-09-16 for the Digitisation phase.

A SEED IS THE SAVE. Generation is a pure function of the world descriptor, so a seed reproduces its world exactly on a given binary; there is no separate snapshot format and none is needed. What a seed cannot carry is why it was chosen, which is what this store holds.

THE FINGERPRINT IS NOT A GOLDEN. It is five counters from seed_library_sweep.json at the repo root, and a world-moving item is SUPPOSED to move them. Re-read with `node tools/session/seed_library.js --check` after such an item, and `--bless` once the movement is authorised. The rationale is the part that survives; the numbers are there so a future session can tell whether the world it generates is still the world described.
THE POOL WAS SWEPT AT PARITY (BL-1007): scripts/world_gen.lua and scripts/works.lua, the shipped data layer. Readings taken before 2026-09-16 describe a different world and do not compare.

To check or bless, regenerate the library's own table first: `build_gen/verify/exploration_sweep.exe --seeds $(node tools/session/seed_library.js --seed-list) --out seed_library_sweep.json` (BL-1026). The checked-in exploration_sweep.json carries seeds 0..15 only and is not the library's table.

A `review` field marks a seed whose rationale is under Ben's review in NEEDS_REVIEW; it names the entry and the candidates, and is removed when he rules. Its `readings` are current; its `why` still describes the world it was chosen as.

pool.config: scripts/world_gen.lua + scripts/works.lua (21 works rows), main at 4c9feb4c

seeds.name: The rich world
seeds.why: The richest world in the pool by a wide margin: a median polity chest of 15.7M against a pool median of about 43k, a top chest of 1.73 billion, 47 post roads (the most) and 7 subjects. If firms cannot form here they cannot form anywhere, so it is the ceiling case for chartering.

seeds.name: The quiet world
seeds.why: The floor case, and the only SILENT seed in 48: fourteen polities, 1,820 Empire battles, two Exploration battles, thirteen trade flows. Digitisation has to produce something legible from almost nothing here.
seeds.review: NR-887: still the floor on breadth (17 polities, 786 corridors, 16 flows — the fewest), but no longer SILENT (41 Exploration battles) and no longer poor (11.5M median chest). Keep, or candidates 28 and 3 for a floor on capital too.

seeds.name: The crowded world
seeds.why: The most crowded: 95 living polities, 19,204 Empire battles, 82 flows and 166 standing treaties, and a median chest of 281. Many poor traders rather than a few rich ones — the hardest case for a firm that needs a treasury behind it.

seeds.name: The trade-dense world
seeds.why: The busiest network in the pool: 94 flows across 77 polities, 5,881 corridors and 166 treaties, with displacement at 8.9. The best world to watch prices form on, because there is already something moving.

seeds.name: The inward world
seeds.why: Wealthy and uninterested: displacement 0.19 (neighbour war leads by five to one), a 521k median chest, 17 post roads and 67 flows. Money and infrastructure without an outward turn — the case where Digitisation must not assume exploration set the table.
seeds.review: NR-887: the reason is gone. It is no longer inward — displacement 1.80, a 127k chest, 9 post roads. Candidates 40 and 39.

seeds.name: The most inward world
seeds.why: The extreme of the same shape: displacement 0.03, 21 flows, a 245 median chest, no subjects. Whatever the phase does here, it does without colonial ties or capital.
seeds.review: NR-887: named for replacement, but the question still holds — inward, no subjects, no capital — and it is now the only SILENT seed in the pool (12 Exploration battles). Keep recommended; candidate 30.

seeds.name: The frontier world
seeds.why: Displacement 459 with zero subjects alive: the conflict moved entirely outward and nobody was subjected by it. A test that trade relationships can form without an overlord graph to inherit.

seeds.name: The colonial world
seeds.why: Eight subjects alive at 1660 with displacement 46 and 62 flows — the densest overlord graph in the pool at this size. The seed for preferred-seller ties, which EXPLORATION hands forward and nothing yet reads.
seeds.review: NR-887: named for replacement. The colonial half holds (7 subjects, tied for the most) but displacement fell to 1.16. Keep recommended; candidates 36 and 20.

seeds.name: The second colonial world
seeds.why: Six subjects and a 281 median chest: colonial ties without the capital behind them, against seed 13 whose chest runs a hundred times deeper.

seeds.name: The small rich world
seeds.why: Twenty-eight polities, a 5.69M median chest and 7 subjects: concentrated wealth in a thin political map. The counterweight to seed 11, and a good world for asking what a company is when there are few of everything.

seeds.name: The paved world
seeds.why: Seventeen post roads, the third most in the pool, yet 35 flows, the fifth-lowest volume and the poorest median chest of all (163). Infrastructure without traffic or capital — the network exists and neither the trade nor the treasury to justify it does.

seeds.name: The roadless traders
seeds.why: The mirror of seed 32: zero post roads, 58 flows and a 144k median chest. Trade that never bought a road, which is the reading BL-949 made recoverable and nobody has explained.

seeds.name: The big busy world
seeds.why: 18,776 Empire battles, 75 polities, 75 flows and 9,030 volume: large, violent and commercial at once. The stress case for whatever Digitisation runs per polity per round.

seeds.name: The insular rich
seeds.why: Twenty-one polities, a 2.24M median chest, displacement 0.2 and sixteen flows. Wealth that stayed home, against seed 6 which is wealth that built roads.
seeds.review: NR-887: the reason is gone. It is neither rich (median chest 285) nor inward (displacement 1.39). Candidates 7 and 38.

seeds.name: The frontier with no neighbours
seeds.why: A no-neighbour-war world: 336 frontier battles, zero neighbour wars, zero subjects, 52 polities. It tests the displacement reading itself as much as the phase — a world satisfied by silence on one axis and busy on the other.
seeds.review: NR-887: the reason is gone. It has neighbours now — 3 neighbour wars, displacement 27.3 — and one subject. Candidates 9 and 16.

seeds.name: The reference world
seeds.why: Seed 0 is the descriptor default and the world every harness, capture and golden is written about; the wizard board capture of 2026-09-16 is this world. It belongs here because a library needs the world everything else is compared against, not because it is unusual.
